 Trump’s $5,000 stimulus check promise faces a big question after Democrats take control of the House and Senate: Will Americans still get the tariff-funded payments?
 SECTIONS Trump’s $5,000 stimulus check promise faces a big question after Democrats take control of the House and Senate: Will Americans still get the tariff-funded payments? By Piyush Shukla , Global Desk Last Updated: Nov 05, 2026, 07:06:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis For Americans who were counting on Donald Trump’s promised $5,000 payment, the midterm election result has raised a big question; will the money still arrive? Trump had promised every adult US citizen a $5,000 check if Republicans retained control of both the House and Senate. That condition has now fallen apart. Democrats have won the Senate and are close to securing a House majority.
 Trump’s $5,000 check promise is now in doubt after Democrats take control of the House and Senate, but does losing Congress mean Americans will miss out on the tariff-funded payments? For many Americans, the question after the midterm elections is not just who will control Congress. It is what happened to the $5,000 check Donald Trump promised them. The US president had tied the payment to one condition; Republicans had to keep control of both chambers. Democrats have now taken the Senate and are close to winning a majority in the House. That has left voters wondering whether the money is still coming.
 Trump first made the promise on September 9 at a Republican midterm convention in Dallas. He repeated it in a November 2 video, saying every adult citizen would receive $5,000 if Republicans won.
 If Republicans win the House of Representatives and the Senate in the 2026 Midterm Elections, I’m going to give all adult citizens in the United States of America, $5,000! Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I look forward to signing those checks! https://t.co/YOkESiUBrc
— Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) October 3, 2026 The proposed payments were expected to come from tariff revenue, but no payment date was announced. With the election result going against his condition, the promise has come under fresh scrutiny. 
 Trump’s $5,000 checks in doubt after Democrats take Congress
Trump announced the plan at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas on September 9. The offer was simple; if the GOP held both chambers, every adult citizen would get $5,000.
He repeated it just before Election Day. On November 2, he posted a video on X saying that if Republicans won, each person would have $5,000 in their pocket, along with economic success “like we have never ever seen before.”
 Live Events
 President Donald Trump promised on Wednesday to send every adult American citizen a $5,000 "dividend" if Republicans keep control of both the Senate and House of Representatives in the midterms."If the Republicans win, you win with us and you get $5,000," Trump told the crowd at the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas. "It will be called the Trump dividend."Trump has proposed other payouts to Americans in the past.During his efforts to cut government spending last year, Elon Musk suggested a "DOGE dividend" of $5,000. Trump said he loved the idea, but it never came to fruition.In a November 2025 post on Truth Social, Trump claimed his tariffs were bringing in trillions of dollars and wrote that a "dividend of at least $2,000 a person (not including high income people!) will be paid to everyone."And in early 2026, more than 1 million U.S. military service members received a "warrior dividend" of $1,776.
— PBS News (@NewsHour) September 10, 2026 The pledge was made in September, repeated on November 2, and the results came in on Tuesday, November 3.
 Voters reacted on X almost at once. One person wrote, “Does this mean I don’t get my $5,000 check?” Another said, “Damn I had plans with that $5,000 check.” A third asked, “So the $5,000 check is up in smokes?”
 Where the money was supposed to come from
The checks were expected to be paid for with tariff revenue. Tariffs are taxes on imported goods, collected by the government. No payment date was ever announced.
Economist Douglas Holtz-Eakin earlier told The U.S. Sun that the plan could have cost more than $1 trillion. That’s a thousand billion dollars. He warned the government would have had to find the money through borrowing or higher taxes.
It wasn’t the first time Trump had floated a payout. He had earlier suggested a $5,000 DOGE dividend and $2,000 tariff rebates. Neither led to nationwide payments.
 Trump blames his absence from the ballot
Trump’s explanation for the losses is that he wasn’t running. He claimed Republicans would have won “IN A LANDSLIDE” if he had been on the ballot. He also said he doesn’t consider the result a defeat, because he “wasn’t on the ballot.”
He called Fox News to talk about the outcome and admitted he was surprised. “I was a little bit surprised,” he said. He had thought he could “transfer those people into candidates.”
He then described how he expects to deal with a Democratic Congress. A veto is a president’s power to reject a bill that Congress has passed, and Trump said he would use it on legislation he opposes. “They’ll send over things that are insane, and I’ll veto them,” he said.
His prediction was that Democrats would come around after a couple of months of vetoes. “They’ll call and they’ll say, ‘How do we get this stuff done?’ And we’ll work together.”
In a separate election-night interview with The New York Times, he said, “I am absolutely willing to accept those results.” He added that he had no regrets about endorsing Republican candidates, even with the party’s losses.
Some of those losses came in Texas. Democrat James Talarico beat Trump-backed Ken Paxton in a major Senate upset. Gina Hinojosa also ousted Republican Governor Greg Abbott.
